title: Wypić czy wyjść?
title_en: The same prefix, two different jobs
note:
B2 Block 6a, unit 3 (spine, JAMES-LOCKED decision #3). REGISTER: authored to James's 2026-08-06 learner-model ruling — the intro names the real categories (prefix, aspect, perfective, imperfective, derivation) rather than the 'front piece / two jobs' framing the earlier prefix units use, and the Polish metalanguage in the slide pl lines (przedrostek, aspekt dokonany, czasownik) is the set already live in a2_aspect and b2_aspect_prefixes. NOTE FOR THE INTRO-REGISTER SWEEP: b2_prefix_lens and b2_motion_imperf one and two nodes back still speak of a 'front piece' and of 'twins', so this unit is currently the odd one out in its own strand until that sweep reaches them — the terminology here is the target, not a local choice. ZERO NEW MATERIAL — teaches_lemmas is empty and every Polish form in the pack is recycled; the unit teaches a DISCRIMINATION, which is why it still declares a structure (prefix_two_jobs) rather than nothing at all: an empty teaches_structures AND teaches_lemmas is what raises the teaches_empty_grammar warn on a2_prep_review and b1_two_futures, and b2_prefix_lens's live precedent is to name the structure and leave the lemma list empty.

THE LANDING LINE THE SPINE DEMANDS is slide 4's, stated in those words: same machinery, two jobs, and you learn which job it is FROM THE PAIR, not from the front piece. It is carried by the wypić/wyjść minimal pair — the same wy- doing the completive job on one verb and the spatial job on the other — which is also the unit's title. That pair is the handoff b2_prefix_lens set up deliberately: that pack excluded wypić from its lens entirely and its note says so, because its wy- is completive rather than spatial and drilling it there would have taught a false meaning.

TITLE CORRECTED from the planned 'Przedrostki · dwie prace', on exactly the b2_prefix_lens precedent: przedrostki is untaught Polish and prace is not owned either (praca/pracy are), and the AGENTS title rule forbids untaught Polish in learner-visible chrome. Retitled to the house pattern on the 'Idę czy jadę?' / 'Wyjść czy przyjść?' model, using two verbs the learner owns. The tree node's label/label_en were updated to match. przedrostek survives only in a body_pl line, the one lane AGENTS allows untaught metalanguage in, as b2_aspect_prefixes and b2_prefix_lens already use it.

b1_two_futures IDIOM, as the spine names it: full ladder (match, quiz, Pisanie, Użycie) rather than b2_prefix_lens's receptive-only shape. Production here is always CHOOSING between two forms the course already taught — never building a prefixed verb — which is the same thing b1_two_futures does with kupię / będę kupować. Pisanie is twelve single-word forms, so the ≤3-word cap is met by construction and no cloze is needed.

NO META-QUESTIONS IN KONTROLA. The spine phrases the task as 'which job is the prefix doing?', which asked literally would be a question ABOUT the language and is banned. Every quiz item is a real form in a real sentence instead, with the job-1 and job-2 candidates sitting side by side as choices; items 7 and 8 are form-choice items on the b2_aspect_prefixes quiz-10 precedent (which taught form is pić's finished half), not metalanguage.

FENCED, and the sharpest call in the unit: pójść and pojechać are NOT used anywhere. po- on iść is aspectual — pójść is iść's perfective, not a directional verb — so it is a case of the same prefix doing job one on a MOTION verb, which is a genuine third fact and would blur the two-way split this unit exists to draw. Logged for C1. Also fenced: any formation rule (b2_aspect_prefixes' 'the piece on the front is unpredictable, learn the pair whole' is restated on slide 3 instead), and za-/po-/prze- as readable prefixes, held to b2_prefix_lens's one-line no-promise treatment.

POOL CATCH worth recording: pisała was drafted as a quiz distractor and REJECTED — b2_aspect_prefixes teaches pisać's past in the first person only (pisałem/pisałam), so the third person is not owned. The item was rebuilt in the first person (napisałem / pisałem). Every Polish token in the pack was checked against the position-aware pool by script, not by eye.

Slide 5 is the one piece of joined-up thinking rather than drill: job two makes a new verb, and job one then gives that new verb its own twin (przyjść → przychodzić), which is why the secondary imperfectives from b2_motion_imperf two nodes back exist at all. It adds no material.

intro.title: A prefix, and the two different jobs it can do
intro.body:
A prefix is the piece on the front of a verb — the wy- in wyjść, the z- in zrobić. You own a great many verbs that carry one, and last unit you learned to read four of them.

This unit exists for the complication that follows. A prefix does not always do the same kind of work.

Sometimes it changes the verb's aspect and nothing else: pić is imperfective, wypić is its perfective. Same activity, now viewed as complete.

Sometimes it derives a different verb altogether: iść is to go, przyjść is to arrive. That is not "iść, completed" — it is a new verb with a meaning of its own.

intro.title: First job — the prefix marks the perfective
intro.body:
These are the aspect pairs you have been collecting since A2, extended two units ago. In each pair the prefix contributes no meaning of its own: it marks the perfective — the same activity, now viewed as complete.

Which prefix a verb takes is not predictable. pisać takes na-, gotować takes u-, jeść takes z-, and there is nothing to work out. The A2 rule stands: learn the pair whole, and never build the perfective out of the imperfective.

One consequence you already know: a perfective verb has no present tense, so its present-shaped forms are future. Zrobię obiad is I will make dinner.

intro.title: Second job — the prefix derives a new verb
intro.body:
Here the prefix does carry meaning, and what comes out is a different verb with its own dictionary entry. przyjść is not "iść, completed" — it is to arrive, which is a separate thing to say.

These are the verbs last unit's reading lens was built for.
intro.body_pl: iść → przyjść · wyjść · dojść · dawać → oddawać

rows: to get all the way there

intro.title: The same prefix doing both — wypić and wyjść
intro.body:
This is why the job cannot be read off the prefix itself. wy- sits on both of these verbs and is doing something different in each.

wypić — wy- marks aspect. The verb still means to drink; it is now perfective.
wyjść — wy- carries meaning. The verb does not mean "to go, completed"; it means to go out.

Same prefix, same machinery, two jobs. So you take the job from the pair itself, not from the prefix: when you meet a new pair, learn what the second verb means rather than deducing it.

examples.en: Dad went out of the office.

intro.title: A derived verb needs an aspect partner of its own
intro.body:
One last point, and it joins the two jobs rather than adding to them.

Once przyjść exists as a verb in its own right, it needs an aspect partner like any other verb — and that is what przychodzić is, which you met two units ago. przyjść is the perfective; przychodzić is the imperfective.

So the second job derives the verb, and the first job then supplies its pair. There is nothing new to learn here: this is why those words exist.

to go out, to leave (on foot)

quiz.prompt: Tata ___ piwo. (Dad drank the beer up — finished it)
quiz.explain: On pić, wy- marks aspect rather than direction — the beer is not going anywhere. wypił says the drinking is complete.

quiz.prompt: Tata ___ z biura o piątej. (went out of the office)
quiz.explain: The same wy- as in wypił, doing the other job: here it carries meaning, and the verb is to go out — away from the office.

quiz.prompt: Mama ___ obiad. (made the dinner — it is ready)
quiz.explain: z- contributes no meaning to robić, only perfective aspect: the dinner is made. The imperfective robiła leaves it in progress.

quiz.prompt: Mama ___ do domu o szóstej. (came home, on foot)
quiz.explain: przy- derives a different verb from iść — to arrive. It is not iść viewed as complete.

quiz.prompt: Wczoraj ___ list. (I wrote the letter — finished it, m)
quiz.explain: na- adds no meaning to pisać, only perfective aspect: the letter is written. The imperfective pisałem leaves it unfinished.

quiz.prompt: Zawsze ___ klucz mamie. (I give the key back)
quiz.explain: od- derives a new verb. Giving something back is not the same act as giving it — daję would just be handing it over.

quiz.prompt: pić → ___ (the twin that means the drinking is finished)
quiz.explain: All four begin with wy-. Only in wypić is that wy- marking aspect; in the other three it carries meaning — out.

quiz.prompt: iść → ___ (a different verb: to go out, to leave)
quiz.explain: Here wy- derives a new verb from iść. Compare wypić, where the very same wy- only marks the perfective.

quiz.prompt: W końcu ___ do banku. (I finally got all the way there, m)
quiz.explain: do- derives a new verb — reaching the place. w końcu is telling you it took some getting to.

quiz.prompt: Jutro ___ zupę. (I will make the soup — one finished job)
quiz.explain: A perfective verb has no present tense, so this present-shaped form is future: zrobię is I will make it. The imperfective robię is I am making it, right now.

quiz.prompt: Jutro ___ z domu o ósmej. (I will leave the house)
quiz.explain: wyjść is perfective, so wyjdę is its future. The same wy- as in wypiję, still doing the other job — out of the house.
